# relgap resolve

Resolves a tool name and prints the result with the layer that supplied each field.

&lt;tool&gt; is a name or alias (terraform, tf), a NAME\_VERSION variable (TERRAFORM\_VERSION),
github:owner/repo, aqua:package, tfprovider:namespace/name, tfmodule:namespace/name/provider,
chart:repo/name, chart:name, chart:url/name, npm:package, pypi:package or action:owner/repo\[/path\].
When a registry knows the tool, the result is the same as for its name. An action:
name resolves to the action's github.com repository and never to a tool a registry lists for it.

tfprovider:, tfmodule:, chart:, npm: and pypi: names that no registry knows are looked up in the
Terraform registry, Artifact Hub, the npm registry or PyPI, which name the source repository. A
module's tag prefix comes from the tag of its latest version. chart:name without a repository
resolves only when one Artifact Hub repository has a chart of that name. chart:url/name names the
chart by its Helm repository URL (https://charts.jetstack.io/cert-manager) and resolves only
through the Artifact Hub repository at that URL, the gh-pages index of a GitHub Pages URL, or the
tags of an oci:// registry relgap reads images from. The short forms tables show,
chart:owner/repo/name for a GitHub Pages URL and chart:registry/path/name for oci://, work too.

Layers, highest precedence first:

```text
config           tools.<name> and aliases in the config file
relgap registry  curated entries embedded in relgap (registry/*.yaml), or the newer copies
                 from 'relgap registry update'
mise registry    mise registry --json when mise is on PATH, otherwise an embedded snapshot
aqua registry    an embedded index of the aqua registry
default          built-in defaults
```

With --guess, a name that no layer knows is searched on GitHub. The repository whose name
matches exactly and has the most stars wins, and the result is marked low-confidence.

## Usage

```sh
relgap resolve <tool> [flags]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Required | Repeatable |
|---|---|---|
| `tool` | yes | no |

## Flags

| Flag | Description | Type | Default | Values | Config key | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--guess` | search GitHub for a tool no registry knows and use the exact name match with the most stars | bool |  |  |  |  |

The [global flags](/cli/global-flags) work with every command.

## Output formats

`--format` accepts `tty`, `plain`, `json`. Without it, the format is `tty` when stdout is a terminal and `plain` otherwise. Formats are described on the [global flags](/cli/global-flags) page.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | The command finished. With --fail-on, nothing matched. |
| 1 | The command failed: a read, a write, a child process or a check failed. |
| 2 | Wrong usage: an unknown command or flag, a bad value or argument, an invalid config file, or a prompt with no terminal. |
| 130 | Interrupted by Ctrl-C (SIGINT) or a cancelled context. |

All codes are listed on the [exit codes](/reference/exit-codes) page.

## Examples

```sh
relgap resolve terraform
relgap resolve TERRAFORM_VERSION
relgap resolve aqua:hashicorp/terraform --format json
relgap resolve tfprovider:integrations/github
relgap resolve tfmodule:terraform-aws-modules/vpc/aws
relgap resolve chart:argo/argo-cd
relgap resolve some-tool --guess
```
